articles.title: Anthropic IPO meets AI backlash after midterms show stinging rebuke of data centers
articles.preview: AI company Anthropic is preparing for a public offering, potentially in mid-November. The company is now targeting a valuation between $1 trillion and $1.5 trillion, reflecting a shift from earlier expectations.

summary.h: Recent Market Trends and Election Results
summary.t: Recent election results indicate a widespread public distrust of tech billionaires and artificial intelligence. Voters favored candidates advocating for stricter AI regulation across several states, including Michigan, Ohio, Texas, and Georgia. Ballot measures related to data centers faced significant opposition, with 40 out of 41 failing. An NBC News exit poll revealed that over half of voters considered AI data centers a crucial factor in their congressional choices. The Nasdaq experienced a significant drop, and October proved to be its worst month since March 2025.

Anthropic is aiming for a Nasdaq debut in mid-November, potentially reaching a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion. This valuation is lower than the previously anticipated $2 trillion. The company, known for its AI models called Claude, primarily serves business clients. Anthropic’s public profile is expected to increase significantly, drawing greater scrutiny due to the current climate surrounding AI.

summary.h: Public Sentiment and Data Center Concerns
summary.t: Public sentiment towards AI has soured, particularly regarding data centers. Concerns revolve around potential environmental harms, rising utility bills, and job displacement.

articles.title: Tech companies face mounting child safety lawsuits while pushing AI into schools
articles.preview: Tech companies are facing a wave of lawsuits related to child safety, with recent settlements and a new lawsuit against Google. Concerns are rising as AI is increasingly integrated into schools, prompting questions about its impact on young users.

summary.t: Snap recently settled a lawsuit confidentially, following previous settlements by Meta, TikTok, and YouTube. A new lawsuit was filed against Google, alleging a child suffered a psychological crisis after using the Gemini AI chatbot in Google Classroom. These cases build upon a broader trend of legal action against tech companies regarding child safety.

Companies are pushing AI into classrooms while seeking trillion-dollar valuations. Developmental psychologist Kate Blocker emphasizes the need for children's safety to be a priority during product design, not an afterthought. Google is facing criticism for linking access to search with the use of its AI tools in schools.

Legal expert Joseph McNally believes these settlements are an attempt by tech companies to improve their image and address legal challenges. Several trials are scheduled to begin in March, and a federal case involving Meta, TikTok, Snap, and YouTube remains active. Plaintiffs are using tactics from social media lawsuits against AI companies like OpenAI.

Meta previously agreed to pay nearly $17 billion to settle a child mental health case with state attorneys general. Anthropic, preparing for an IPO, acknowledged potential litigation risks related to child safety in its prospectus.

articles.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
articles.preview: Despite voter opposition to data centers, OpenAI plans to continue investing in AI infrastructure. The company is also pursuing a potential public debut around 2027, even as a rival prepares to go public sooner.

summary.t: OpenAI's CFO, Sarah Friar, stated the company will proceed with investments in AI infrastructure. This decision comes despite voters rejecting or restricting data centers in 40 out of 41 ballot measures across 10 states. Friar emphasized the need to meet customer demand and maintain relationships with major cloud providers.
OpenAI recently released a policy blueprint for data centers. They are committed to engaging with communities and building trust.

articles.title: OpenAI bugging suspect Alfozan pleads not guilty
articles.preview: A Saudi national pleaded not guilty to planting a listening device at OpenAI headquarters. Abdulrahman Alfozan was ordered to remain in jail until his next court appearance on November 17th.

summary.t: Abdulrahman Alfozan, aged 35, entered a not guilty plea on Friday. He is accused of intercepting oral communications, a single count. He remains in custody without bail.

articles.title: Investors brace for lower Anthropic valuation, calling $1.5 trillion a 'stretch'
articles.preview: Investors are now questioning Anthropic's potential valuation, moving away from earlier expectations. A $1.5 trillion valuation is now considered unlikely, with some suggesting a range closer to $1 trillion.

summary.t: Anthropic, an AI company, is preparing for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. Investors previously anticipated a valuation of $2 trillion, then $1.5 trillion, but now consider that figure a 'stretch.' A valuation between $1 trillion and $1.25 trillion is now more likely.
Recent market declines, including a 5% drop in the Nasdaq, are fueling the change in sentiment.

articles.title: Microsoft plans to use fewer neoclouds as AI buildout shows signs of strain
articles.preview: Microsoft is reducing its partnerships with neocloud providers, shifting focus to its own data centers. This change highlights growing concerns about the financial stability of the AI infrastructure market.

summary.t: Microsoft is reevaluating its relationships with several neocloud partners. The company intends to prioritize its own data center infrastructure. This move follows a period of collaboration with companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Oracle. Two sources indicated that Microsoft did not renew its deal with Oracle.

The neocloud market faces challenges due to rising interest rates and debt loads. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN have dropped significantly. Industry analysts predict that many of the 323 existing neoclouds may not survive.
Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases. Some cloud contracts involving GPUs have been delayed until 2027.

articles.title: OpenAI, Arm and Qualcomm executives react to post-midterm AI sell-off
articles.preview: Tech stocks experienced a significant sell-off following the midterm elections, wiping out over $1 trillion in market value. Executives from OpenAI, Arm, and Qualcomm addressed investor concerns about potential data center limitations and the future of AI.

summary.t: Following the midterm elections, markets initially rallied on Wednesday, marking their best day in over 18 months. This positive trend reversed quickly on Thursday with a sharp sell-off as investors worried about data center slowdowns and a possible peak in the AI trade. The 'Magnificent Seven' tech companies collectively lost over $1 trillion in market capitalization.

Arm CEO, Rene Haas, dismissed the post-election concerns as short-sighted. He emphasized the importance of continued U.S. investment in data centers to avoid falling behind other countries. Haas noted significant global demand for this capacity.
OpenAI plans to continue investing in data center infrastructure despite voter rejections of data centers.

articles.title: Marktbericht: Zweifel am KI-Geschäft belasten die Branche
articles.preview: An den Börsen weltweit gibt es Kursverluste bei Technologie- und Chipwerten, was Zweifel an KI-Investitionen aufwirft. Der geplante Börsengang von Anthropic steht zudem aufgrund von Skepsis gegenüber der Bewertung im Fokus.

summary.t: Nach den Midterm-Wahlen in den USA, bei denen die Demokraten die Mehrheit erlangten, kommt es zu einem deutlichen Abverkauf von Technologieaktien. Dies betrifft nicht nur die USA, sondern auch Asien und Frankfurt. Der Handel in Südkorea musste zeitweise unterbrochen werden. Die Demokraten zeigen eine skeptischere Haltung gegenüber Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) als die bisherige Regierung, was zu Befürchtungen einer stärkeren Regulierung führt. Finanzexpertin Lisa Hassenzahl warnt vor den Folgen dieser politischen Veränderung.

Bereits vor den Wahlen gab es Widerstand gegen den Bau neuer Rechenzentren, auch von republikanischen Politikern. Die Bedenken drehen sich um den hohen Stromverbrauch, Lärm, Luftverschmutzung, Wasserknappheit und die wenigen Arbeitsplätze. Zusätzlich werden höhere Abgaben auf KI-Gewinne in den USA diskutiert. Die Sorgen um die Tech-Branche zeigen sich in Kursverlusten bei Unternehmen wie Infineon, Siemens Energy und Hochtief.

Der geplante Börsengang des KI-Unternehmens Anthropic gerät nun in Frage. Potenzielle Investoren äußern Zweifel an der Bewertung von 1,5 Billionen US-Dollar und drängen auf einen niedrigeren Preis. Die anhaltenden Quartalsverluste und die hohen finanziellen Verpflichtungen des Unternehmens tragen zu dieser Skepsis bei. Die Umsatzzahlen für Oktober, die im Börsenprospekt fehlten, werden nun von Investoren erwartet. Eine Verschiebung des Börsengangs könnte die gesamte KI-Branche belasten.

articles.title: Chinese AI lab Moonshot turned to Europe for Nvidia Blackwell access amid U.S. China curbs, sources tell CNBC
articles.preview: A Chinese AI lab, Moonshot AI, is seeking Nvidia chip access through European data centers. This move circumvents U.S. export controls designed to limit China's AI advancements.

summary.t: Moonshot AI, a Chinese lab previously flagged for accessing Nvidia chips remotely, is now exploring options to rent computing capacity from European data centers. These centers host Nvidia GPUs, allowing Moonshot to potentially bypass U.S. export controls. The White House previously noted Moonshot accessed Blackwell chips through a facility in Thailand. Current regulations lack authority over cloud-based access hosted overseas.

summary.h: The AI Race and Moonshot's Growth
summary.t: Nvidia’s dominance in advanced chips makes U.S. export controls a key tool in the AI competition. Moonshot AI, founded in 2023, has rapidly gained prominence, releasing a model in July that rivals those from Anthropic and OpenAI. Increased access to Nvidia chips could intensify pressure on American AI developers. Demand for Moonshot’s models has been so high that subscriptions were temporarily paused.
Discussions have involved leasing clusters with 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs in Europe.

articles.title: Insider: Zweifel an Werbetour: Börsengang von Anthropic wackelt
articles.preview: Der geplante Börsengang von Anthropic, bekannt für den Chatbot Claude, könnte sich verzögern. Investoren äußern Bedenken bezüglich der Bewertung und warten auf weitere Informationen.

summary.t: Nach den Midterm-Wahlen fallen Tech-Aktien an der Wall Street. Dies führt zu Unsicherheit und einem starken Ausverkauf von Technologieunternehmen.
Die Werbetour für einen Börsengang im November steht nun auf der Kippe.

articles.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
articles.preview: OpenAI is collaborating with Hacktron. This partnership aims to improve system security.

articles.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
articles.preview: OpenAI released BioBasicsBench, a new benchmark. It assesses AI agents' abilities in wet-lab science.

articles.title: AI meltdown: Nvidia and Qualcomm drop more than 9%, pushing Nasdaq to worst day since April 2025
articles.preview: Chipmakers experienced a significant downturn on Thursday, impacting the Nasdaq's performance. Nvidia's stock dropped sharply, resulting in a loss of nearly $450 billion in market capitalization.

summary.t: Chipmaker stocks plummeted following the midterm election results. Concerns arose regarding a potential slowdown in the artificial intelligence buildout. The Nasdaq suffered its largest decline in 19 months, dropping 5.5%. This downturn is attributed to rising interest rates, capital needs, and the Democratic sweep in Congress, leading to fears of excessive debt and insufficient revenue.

Nvidia and Qualcomm both experienced drops exceeding 9%, with Nvidia losing almost $450 billion in market cap. Qualcomm issued a disappointing earnings forecast, citing supply chain issues. Other chipmakers, including Advanced Micro Devices, Micron, and Applied Materials, also saw double-digit percentage losses. Even companies like Tesla and SpaceX, linked to Elon Musk, faced declines.

articles.title: Democrat shaping AI policy bought chip stocks despite backing congressional trading ban
articles.preview: Representative Josh Gottheimer, involved in crafting Democratic AI policy, recently purchased AI-related stocks. This occurred despite his prior support for a congressional trading ban.

summary.t: Representative Josh Gottheimer has disclosed recent purchases of stocks linked to artificial intelligence. These include between $1,001 and $15,000 of Benchmark Electronics, and up to $15,000 of Applied Materials. He also made earlier purchases of Advanced Micro Devices, a leading AI chipmaker.

Gottheimer, a former Microsoft executive, plays a key role in shaping Democratic AI policy. He sits on a subcommittee and has introduced AI-related legislation. Democrats are now preparing to regulate and investigate the AI industry.
A spokesman states Gottheimer delegated investment control to a third party in 2017.

articles.title: Musk spendete Rekordsumme: Amerikas Tech-Oligarchen regieren trotz Wahldebakel weiter mit
articles.preview: Elon Musk investierte fast 500 Millionen Dollar in den republikanischen Wahlkampf und verlor. Trotz des Demokratensiegs bleiben Tech-Milliardäre langfristig wahrscheinlich die Gewinner.

summary.t: Elon Musk hat rund 500 Millionen Dollar in den republikanischen Wahlkampf investiert. Dies stellt die höchste Spende eines Einzelnen in einem US-Wahlkampf dar. Im Vergleich zu seinem Vermögen von fast einer Billion Dollar, entspricht dies etwa 0,05 Prozent. Trotz seiner Investition haben die Demokraten die Wahl gewonnen. Musk kann sich diese Niederlage leisten und die politischen Machtverschiebungen im Kongress werden für ihn wahrscheinlich verkraftbar bleiben.

Die Wähler haben die Allianz zwischen Trump und Tech-Oligarchen abgestraft. Der Kongress kann nun Trumps Ernennungen blockieren und es könnten Ermittlungen zu seinen Kryptogeschäften und Musks Rolle in einer Effizienzbehörde geben. Die neue demokratische Gouverneurin von Texas, Gina Hinojosa, hat Klage gegen Musk eingereicht, um Einblick in seine politischen Absprachen zu erhalten.

Das Ziel der Tech-Milliardäre, Technologie zur Einschränkung demokratischer Mitbestimmung einzusetzen, bleibt bestehen. Sie wollen die Welt von ihren Konzernen abhängig machen. Der Machtwechsel im Kongress ist lediglich ein Anfang, um die US-Demokratie wieder aufzubauen. US-Präsidenten haben nach ihrer Amtszeit juristischen Schutz. Kurzfristig hält Trump seine Unterstützung für die Tech-Milliardäre aufrecht und könnte sie vor Strafverfolgung begnadigen.
Wenige Politiker fordern eine Regulierung von KI oder eine Reichensteuer. In Kalifornien scheitert eine Milliardärssteuer wahrscheinlich.

articles.title: Nasdaq legt zu: KI-Werte erholen sich vom Kursgemetzel
articles.preview: Die KI-Aktien erholen sich nach Kursverlusten. Der Nasdaq legte zu, während der Dow Jones schwächer endete.

summary.t: Nach deutlichen Kursverlusten, ausgelöst durch die US-Zwischenwahlen, erholten sich KI-Aktien am Freitag. Anleger nutzten den Rückgang als Kaufgelegenheit. Besonders Halbleiterkonzerne profitierten davon.
Der technologielastige Nasdaq stieg um 1,1 Prozent auf 24.579 Punkte. Der S&P 500 gewann 0,3 Prozent und erreichte 7377 Zähler.

articles.title: Cramer’s week ahead: AI data center stocks face another hurdle and so does the Fed
articles.preview: Next week's earnings reports from cloud companies could challenge investor confidence in the data center sector. Jim Cramer anticipates potential challenges for the Federal Reserve due to inflation data and company financing concerns.

summary.t: Following a turbulent election week, the market saw a rebound on Friday, but Jim Cramer remains wary. He believes the recovery might be a 'dead cat bounce,' suggesting lingering sellers await a larger market improvement. Investors will be closely watching earnings reports from several companies to gauge the health of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Constellation Energy and Nebius will release reports early in the week, offering insights into the impact of political uncertainty on data center infrastructure. CoreWeave, a heavily indebted cloud provider, will report after the market close, needing to address financing and borrowing cost concerns. On Holding’s athletic footwear earnings are also expected, but Cramer is skeptical.

articles.title: AI stocks hammered by midterm shock as data center buildout becomes a 'war of attrition'
articles.preview: Midterm election results caused significant volatility in AI and tech stocks, with major companies experiencing substantial sell-offs. Concerns over potential regulation and slowing AI spending are contributing to investor uncertainty.

summary.t: The unexpected strength of Democrats in the midterm elections triggered a sharp downturn in tech and AI stocks. On Thursday, major companies like Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, and Tesla saw significant losses, with Nvidia dropping 9.3% and AMD losing 17.3%. This market reaction reflects investor anxieties about potential regulatory hurdles and a slowdown in the AI boom.

Several ballot measures across ten states aim to restrict data center construction, adding to existing challenges. Between January 2024 and May 2026, over $170 billion in announced AI data center investment faced roadblocks. Analysts believe the midterm results will likely slow the planned construction of 800 to 1,000 data centers across the U.S.

The stock declines follow a disappointing earnings season, where many companies’ results fell short of expectations. Goldman Sachs estimates AI-related capital spending could reach $7.6 trillion between 2026 and 2031. However, concerns about rising interest rates and overspending have already impacted the sector, with some hyperscalers experiencing negative cash flow.
Analysts now predict that the peak of Big Tech capital expenditure growth will occur in 2027, a shift from previous estimates.

articles.title: Weltweiter KI-Ausverkauf: DAX rutscht nach Rekordhoch ab
articles.preview: Der DAX hat nach einem Rekordhoch deutlich nachgegeben. Ein weltweiter Ausverkauf von KI- und Halbleiteraktien belastet den deutschen Aktienmarkt.

summary.t: Der DAX ist am 6. November 2026 nach einem Rekordhoch von 26.692 Punkten gefallen. Nach Handelsbeginn ging es um knapp zwei Prozent abwärts. Der Leitindex schloss schließlich bei rund 25.820 Punkten, was einem Verlust von 1,9 Prozent entspricht. Damit gab der DAX sein Wochenplus auf.

Die Abverkäufe begannen an der Wall Street und breiteten sich auf asiatische Börsen aus. In Seoul musste der Handel kurzzeitig ausgesetzt werden. Auch in den USA erholten sich die Börsen teilweise wieder, wobei der Nasdaq 100 rund neun Prozent seit Ende Oktober eingebüßt hat. Der Dow Jones gab leicht nach.
Die Anleger äußern wachsende Zweifel, ob sich die Investitionen in Künstliche Intelligenz auszahlen werden.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Tech-Boom ausgebremst - so können Anleger trotzdem profitieren
articles.preview: Der KI-Boom an der Börse verlangsamt sich aktuell. Hohe Zinsen wirken sich dabei aus.

articles.title: The AI ‘credit card’ is getting costlier as CoreWeave bond yield tops 16%
articles.preview: Debt markets are signaling increased costs for companies building AI data centers, with CoreWeave's bond yield exceeding 16%. This shift reflects concerns about potential regulatory hurdles and impacts investor confidence.

summary.t: Investors are now demanding higher compensation to protect against potential defaults, even for companies with strong financial standings. CoreWeave's 2032 bond yield has surpassed 16%, and its credit default swaps spiked above 1,289 basis points. This trend extends to major players like Nvidia, Broadcom, and Amazon, with their CDS increasing significantly in recent weeks.

The recent election results, with Democratic governors in key states like Ohio, Texas, and Georgia, have introduced uncertainty. These governors may implement moratoriums on data center construction, potentially impacting 45% of planned U.S. capacity, especially in Texas. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has expressed a desire for a moratorium until community protections are in place.

Despite the concerns, significant AI-related debt issuance continues. Goldman Sachs reports $67 billion in AI bond deals since October 29, bringing this year's total to $296 billion, with a forecast of $440 billion next year.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Nasdaq deutlich im Plus - Tech-Aktien grün
articles.preview: Die US-Börsen erholen sich teilweise von gestern. Der Nasdaq gewinnt 1,4 Prozent.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Allgemeines Risk-Off an Börsen - umgekehrt Plus bei Chipwerten
articles.preview: Europäische Börsen zeigen Kursverluste. Chipwerte weisen jedoch einen Anstieg auf.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: "Blutbad" bei Tech-Aktien - was hat Politik damit zu tun?
articles.preview: Nach dem Wahlsieg der Demokraten sind Tech-Aktien stark gefallen. Investoren befürchten neue Regulierungen und Probleme bei Rechenzentren.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: KI-Aktien erholen sich - hier eine Liste
articles.preview: Die Technologieaktien erholen sich im vorbörslichen Handel. Es folgte gestern ein Ausverkauf an der Wall Street.

articles.title: Nasdaq sell-off batters Asian chip stocks as SK Hynix, Samsung, Softbank, TSMC tumble
articles.preview: Asian technology stocks experienced a significant decline Friday, mirroring a Wall Street sell-off. Concerns about AI spending and potential U.S. policy changes fueled the downturn.

summary.t: Several South Korean companies saw substantial losses. SK Hynix dropped 10.44% and Samsung Electronics fell 6.35%. LG Innotek and LG Display also experienced declines of 7.02% and 4.45%, respectively.
Japanese semiconductor-related stocks also suffered.

articles.title: Chipaktien an den internationalen Börsen im freien Fall
articles.preview: Chip- und Technologieaktien erleben weltweit einen starken Kursverlust, der wichtige Aktienindizes belastet. In Südkorea musste der Handel zeitweise ausgesetzt werden, während in den USA der schlimmste Einbruch seit 2020 verzeichnet wurde.

summary.t: Ein weltweiter Abverkauf von Chip- und Technologieaktien hat zu einem deutlichen Kursverlust an den internationalen Börsen geführt. Besonders betroffen sind die USA, Südkorea und Deutschland. In Seoul wurde der Handel für 20 Minuten unterbrochen, während in den USA der stärkste Einbruch seit März 2020 verzeichnet wurde.

Der Kursrutsch an der Wall Street, wo Technologie- und Chipkonzerne Milliardenverluste verzeichneten, löste die Verkaufswelle aus. Investoren äußern zunehmende Zweifel, ob sich die Investitionen in Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) und Rechenzentren auszahlen werden. Die Wahlergebnisse in den USA könnten zudem zu strengeren Regulierungen führen.
Experten wie Stephan Kemper von BNP Paribas warnen vor möglichen Problemen, wenn Genehmigungen für den Bau von Rechenzentren und die Stromversorgung stocken.

articles.title: Panikverkäufe wegen KI und Öl : Börsen in Fernost sacken ab - TSMC, Samsung und SK Hynix leiden
articles.preview: Asiatische Aktienmärkte erleben starke Verkäufe. Der südkoreanische Leitindex Kospi ist um über acht Prozent gefallen.

summary.t: Die Verkaufswelle von den US-Börsen hat sich auf Asien ausgeweitet. Dies geschieht aufgrund von Sorgen über eine verstärkte Regulierung von Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) nach den US-Zwischenwahlen.
Der Kospi-Index fiel im Frühhandel um fast neun Prozent. Er unterbot erstmals seit Februar die 5.000-Punkte-Marke, stabilisierte sich später aber leicht.
In Taiwan belastete das Schwergewicht TSMC die Kurse.

articles.title: Jim Cramer explains why no AI stock seems safe from the market carnage
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes uncertainty around data center construction is impacting AI stock valuations, leading to recent selling. He suggests even seemingly cheap stocks like Nvidia face risk if growth forecasts don't materialize.

summary.t: AI stocks have experienced significant selling over the last two days. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) dropped 3% on Wednesday and 10% on Thursday. GE Vernova and Sandisk saw declines of 7% and 22%, respectively, on Thursday.
A key factor is uncertainty regarding the future of data center construction. Regulatory hurdles and opposition to new centers could slow build-out.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says the AI sell-off isn't over, but it isn't another dot-com crash
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes the recent decline in AI stocks is likely to continue, but he doesn't see it as a repeat of the dot-com crash. He advises investors to hold cash and remain calm, suggesting a quick sell-off could be beneficial.

summary.t: AI-related stocks have experienced a significant sell-off. Micron fell 17%, GE Vernova dropped 7%, and Sandisk plunged 22% on Thursday, following similar declines on Wednesday. Jim Cramer, from CNBC, predicts further declines are possible.

Growing opposition to new data centers, particularly after the midterm elections, is impacting investor sentiment. This has raised doubts about future spending on AI infrastructure, driving down stock prices.
